gloss: be whole, complete; come to an end; whole, without blemish; integrity
summary: The verb is to be whole or complete, and so to come to its end: a task finished, a sum spent, a generation consumed (Deu 31:24; Gen 47:18; Deu 2:14–16). תָּמִים is whole, lacking nothing: an offering with no blemish in it (Lev 22:21), a whole day or year, “seven complete sabbaths” (Lev 23:15), and a man undivided toward God, as Noah and Job were and as Abraham is told to be (Gen 6:9; 17:1; Job 1:1). תֹּם and תֻּמָּה are that wholeness of heart, integrity, which Job holds fast (Job 2:3, 9); the Thummim of the high priest’s breastpiece bear the same name. Arabic tamma and Punic tmm have the same sense of complete and of a life lived uprightly.

words.gloss: whole, complete; without blemish; whole-hearted, blameless
words.summary: Whole, with nothing lacking or marred: of an animal for the altar, of a span of time, of a person’s walk with God, and of God’s own way, work and law. Two-thirds of its uses are offerings, almost all in Leviticus, Numbers and Ezekiel.

senses.definition: An animal with no defect in it, as the altar requires; the opposite of one with a מוּם, blemish.

evidence.note: “It shall be תָּמִים to be accepted; there shall be no מוּם in it.”
“A תָּמִים male of the cattle, the sheep or the goats.”
“Whatever has a מוּם you shall not offer, for it will not be accepted for you.”
A red heifer “תְּמִימָה, in which there is no מוּם”.
The Passover lamb: “a שֶׂה תָמִים, a male a year old”.
The burnt offering, “a תָּמִים male”.
The sin offering of the anointed priest.
On the day of the waving of the עֹמֶר, “a lamb תָּמִים a year old for a burnt offering to Yahweh”.
With the new grain offering, seven lambs תְּמִימִם a year old.
The continual burnt offering, two lambs a day.
In Ezekiel’s house, a goat תָּמִים for a sin offering.

senses.gloss: whole, complete (of time or a thing)
senses.definition: Entire, full: a whole day, a full year, a count of weeks with none short; a thing still whole, not yet broken or burnt.

evidence.note: From the morrow after the sabbath, the day the עֹמֶר is brought, “seven sabbaths, תְּמִימֹת they shall be”: seven full weeks to the fiftieth day.
If a house in a walled city is not redeemed “until a שָׁנָה תְמִימָה is fulfilled”.
The sun did not hasten to go down “about a whole day”, כְּיוֹם תָּמִים.
The vine’s wood: “when it was תָּמִים it was not made into anything”, much less when the fire has eaten it.
“Let us swallow them alive like Sheol, and תְמִימִים like those who go down to the pit”: whole.

senses.definition: Of a person, undivided and sound in their dealings with God and men: walking before him with nothing held back from him, not without faults but without falseness.

evidence.note: “I am אֵל שַׁדַּי; walk before me and be תָמִים.”
“Noah was a righteous man, תָּמִים in his generations; Noah walked with God.”
“You shall be תָּמִים with Yahweh your God”, set against seeking diviners and the dead (Deu 18:9–14): undivided loyalty.
“Fear Yahweh and serve him בְּתָמִים וּבֶאֱמֶת, and put away the gods your fathers served.”
Jotham: if you have acted בֶּאֱמֶת וּבְתָמִים in making Abimelech king.
Who may dwell on your holy hill? “He who walks תָּמִים and does righteousness and speaks truth in his heart.”
“I was תָמִים with him, and I kept myself from my iniquity”: wholeness is keeping oneself from sin, not having none.
“I will walk in the way תָּמִים … in the integrity (תָּם) of my heart.”
“Blessed are the תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ, who walk in the law of Yahweh.”
“Let my heart be תָמִים in your statutes.”
The crooked of heart are an abomination to Yahweh, but the תְמִימֵי דָרֶךְ are his delight.
He who walks תָמִים will be saved, but the crooked will fall.
To the king of Tyre: “You were תָּמִים in your ways from the day you were created, until iniquity was found in you.”
They abhor him who speaks תָּמִים.
“The righteous, the תָּמִים, a laughingstock.”

senses.gloss: perfect, whole (of God, his work, way and law)
senses.definition: Of God’s work, way, knowledge and law: whole, with nothing wrong or lacking in it.

evidence.note: “The Rock, his work is תָּמִים, for all his ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without injustice.”
“As for God, his way is תָּמִים; the word of Yahweh is tried.” Also 2Sa 22:31.
He girds me with strength “and makes my way תָמִים”.
“The law of Yahweh is תְּמִימָה, restoring the soul.”
The wondrous works of תְּמִים דֵּעִים, him who is perfect in knowledge.

senses.definition: In Saul’s prayer at the lot: “give תָמִים”; the word’s sense here is not certain.

evidence.note: Saul to Yahweh: “הָבָה תָמִים”, “give a whole/true [answer]”, and Jonathan and Saul are taken by lot. Some read here the Thummim (see תֹּם); the Hebrew has the adjective.

parallels.note: “Righteous”, beside it of Noah and of Job’s friend.
“Faithfulness, truth”: serving or acting בְּתָמִים וּבֶאֱמֶת.

opposites.note: A blemish, which disqualifies an animal that is not תָּמִים.
“Crooked, perverse”, against those whole in their way.

evidence.locator: Lev.22.21, תָּמִים → ἄμωμον; Lev.1.3 the same; ἄμωμος renders תָּמִים ×65

evidence.note: Redeemed “with precious blood, as of a lamb ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου, of Christ”: the תָּמִים lamb.
Christ “offered himself ἄμωμον to God”.
The church to be presented holy and ἄμωμος.

evidence.locator: Gen.6.9, תָּמִים → τέλειος; Exo.12.5, תָמִים → τέλειον; τέλειος renders תָּמִים ×4

evidence.note: “You shall be τέλειοι, as your heavenly Father is τέλειος”, closing the command to love enemies (Mat 5:44–47); the wording “you shall be τέλειος” is the Septuagint’s for Deu 18:13.

words.gloss: be complete, be finished, come to an end; be whole
words.summary: Mostly qal, of something reaching its full measure and so its end: work done, words finished, money spent, people consumed. A few uses keep the sense of being whole or blameless, as the adjective has it (Psa 19:14; 2Sa 22:26).

stems.gloss: be complete, be finished; be spent, consumed; be whole

senses.gloss: be finished, come to an end
senses.definition: Of an action, a span of time or a speech reaching its end.

evidence.note: When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book “until they were תֻּמָּם”.
Until all the nation had completely crossed the Jordan.
When they had finished circumcising all the nation.
The days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.
The whole house overlaid with gold, until all the house was finished.
The work of the pillars was finished.
Until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah.
Redemption of a house sold “until a year from its sale is complete”.
“The words of Job are ended.”
“Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion; he will no more exile you.”

senses.definition: Of a store run out, or people consumed to the last.

evidence.note: “The silver is spent (תַּם), and the herds of cattle are my lord’s.”
Thirty-eight years, “until all the generation of the men of war had perished from the camp”.
Your children will wander forty years “until your carcases are consumed in the wilderness”.
Sword, famine and plague “until they are consumed from the land”.
“Your strength shall be spent in vain.”
The enemy has come to an end.
Let sinners be consumed from the earth.
“The mercies of Yahweh, that we are not consumed (לֹא תָמְנוּ)”, or, as the next line reads, that “they do not come to an end”.
“You are the same, and your years will not תַּמּוּ”: have no end; quoted in Heb 1:12.

senses.definition: Be whole toward God, kept from great transgression.

evidence.note: “Keep your servant from presumptuous sins; let them not rule over me; then אֵיתָם, and I shall be innocent of great transgression.”

stems.gloss: complete, finish; bring to an end; make whole

senses.gloss: complete, finish, bring to an end
senses.definition: Finish a matter or a reckoning; finish doing something; bring something wholly to an end.

evidence.note: Let Hilkiah “sum up” the silver brought into the house of Yahweh.
“When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed.”
“They used to say, Let them ask at Abel, and so they settled it.”
“I will consume your uncleanness out of you”, by scattering among the nations.
“Boil the flesh well.”
In the latter time of their kingdom, “when the transgressors have come to the full”.

senses.definition: Make one’s ways whole.

evidence.note: “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous, or gain that you make your ways whole (תַתֵּם)?”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, to deal wholly with the one who is whole toward him.

evidence.note: “With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the man who is תָּמִים you show yourself whole (תִּתַּמָּם).”

words.summary: The wholeness תָּמִים describes, mostly of the heart: integrity, set beside uprightness and against crookedness. The plural תֻּמִּים is the Thummim, kept with the Urim in the high priest’s breastpiece. BDB’s key also counts some infinitives of the verb, “until the finishing of …” (Lev 25:29; Jos 4:10; Jer 36:23), which are cited under the verb.

senses.definition: A heart or walk that is whole and without falseness; what a person may appeal to God by.

evidence.note: Abimelech: “In the תָם of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this”; God answers, “I know that you did this in the תָם of your heart” (Gen 20:6).
“If you will walk before me as David your father walked, בְּתָם לֵבָב וּבְיֹשֶׁר.”
“Let תֹּם and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you.”
“Judge me, Yahweh, for I have walked in my תֹּם, and I have trusted in Yahweh without wavering.”
“Judge me … according to my righteousness and my תֹּם.”
David shepherded them according to the תֹּם of his heart.
He who walks בַּתֹּם walks securely; he who perverts his ways will be found out.
Better a poor man walking in his תֹּם than one perverse of lips.
Eliphaz: “Is not your fear your confidence, and the תֹּם of your ways your hope?”

senses.definition: Acting with a whole and simple mind, not knowing what lies behind; at random.

evidence.note: Two hundred men went with Absalom “in their תֹּם, and knew nothing at all”.
A man drew his bow לְתֻמּוֹ, “in his simplicity”, at random, and struck the king of Israel.

senses.definition: The full measure or full strength of something.

evidence.note: Loss of children and widowhood will come on Babylon כְּתֻמָּם, “in their full measure”.
One dies “in his full strength” (בְּעֶצֶם תֻּמּוֹ), wholly at ease.

senses.definition: With the Urim, the things put in the high priest’s breastpiece of judgment, over his heart before Yahweh, by which judgment was given; the name is the plural of תֹּם, “wholenesses”.

evidence.note: “You shall put in the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be on Aaron’s heart when he goes in before Yahweh.”
Moses puts them in the breastpiece at Aaron’s consecration.
Moses’ blessing of Levi: “Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one.”
Some may not eat of the most holy things “until a priest stands up with Urim and with Thummim”.

words.summary: A shorter adjective of the same sense as תָּמִים, used chiefly of Job and in Proverbs, Psalms and the Song.

senses.definition: Of a person, whole and upright, set beside יָשָׁר and against the wicked.

evidence.note: “That man was תָּם וְיָשָׁר, fearing God and turning from evil.”
“God will not reject a תָּם man.”
“If I were תָּם, it would prove me perverse.”
“He destroys the תָּם and the wicked”, set against each other.
“Mark the תָּם and behold the upright, for the end of that man is peace.”
Shooting in secret at the תָּם.
Men of blood hate the תָּם.
“Esau was a man skilled in hunting, a man of the field, and Jacob was an אִישׁ תָּם, dwelling in tents”: set against Esau’s wild life; quiet, settled.

senses.definition: Of the bride in the Song: without flaw.

evidence.note: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, תַמָּתִי.”
“My dove, my תַמָּתִי, is one.” Compare Sng 4:7: “there is no מוּם in you”.

senses.definition: Of the corner boards of the tabernacle, joined whole at the top; the sense is uncertain, and some take it from תאם “twin”.

evidence.note: “They shall be doubled (תֹאֲמִם) beneath, and together they shall be תַמִּים at its top.”

senses.definition: Wholeness of a person toward God, held fast through suffering.

evidence.note: Yahweh: “he still holds fast his תֻּמָּה, although you moved me against him.”
His wife: “Do you still hold fast your תֻּמָּה? Curse God and die.”
“Until I die I will not put away my תֻּמָּה from me.”
“Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my תֻּמָּה.”
“The תֻּמַּת of the upright guides them, but the crookedness of the treacherous destroys them.”

words.summary: Wholeness of the body, always negated: “there is no מְתֹם”. BDB’s key also counts מְתִם “men” (Deu 2:34; 3:6), another word, and Jdg 20:48, which is uncertain.

senses.definition: A body whole and unhurt; said of Israel struck from head to foot, and of the psalmist under God’s anger.

evidence.note: “From the sole of the foot to the head there is no מְתֹם in it: wounds and bruises and raw sores.”
“There is no מְתֹם in my flesh because of your indignation.”
If it belongs here: Israel struck “from the city, מְתֹם, to the beast”, the city whole; others read מְתִם, its men.

words.summary: The Peshitta uses it for Greek ἀκέραιος, “unmixed, guileless”, and ἄμωμος, “without blemish”.

senses.definition: Whole and simple, with no mixture of evil in it.

evidence.note: “Be wise as serpents and תַּמִּימֵא as doves.”
Wise toward what is good, and תַּמִּימֵא toward evil.
“That you may be without blame and תַּמִּימֵא, children of God without blemish, in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation”, the words of Deu 32:5.

cognates.gloss: be complete, entire, whole, without deficiency; tāmm complete, whole, perfect; tamīm complete in make, strong
cognates.note: Lane’s sources gloss تَمَامٌ as a thing’s “being without deficiency”; تَامُّ الخَلْقِ is a man complete in his members, and the moon is said تَمَّ when full. Form IV أَتَمَّ is to complete, II تَمَّمَ also “make to reach its appointed term”, as Hebrew תַּם is “come to its end”.

evidence.note: “[The thing was, or became, complete, entire, whole, or full; i. e., without, or free from, deficiency: and sometimes, the thing was, or became, consummate, or perfect]”; form II “He, or it, destroyed it; made it to reach its appointed term of duration”.
تَامٌّ “Complete, entire, whole, or full; without, or free from, deficiency: and consummate, or perfect”; تَمِيمٌ “complete, or perfect, in make, or formation, and strong”.

cognates.gloss: be good, live uprightly; be deemed good; (yiphil) complete
cognates.note: Neo-Punic epitaphs say of the dead tm bḥym, “he was whole/good in his lifetime”, which the Latin of bilingual stones renders vixit honeste: the same use as תָּם and תָּמִים of a person’s walk. The yiphil “complete” a building matches the Hebrew verb.

evidence.note: “v. qal 1. BE GOOD, LIVE RIGHTEOUSLY, KAI 152.3 (NPu) tm bḥym, ‘He was good during his lifetime’ = Latin vixit honeste … 2. BE DEEMED GOOD/APPROPRIATE, KAI 60 … v. yiphʿil COMPLETE, KAI 124.2/4”.

cognates.note: The Targum of Proverbs uses it where the Hebrew has תָּם and תָּמִים (Targ. Pro 13:6; 28:10).

evidence.note: “Targ. Y. II, Lev. XXII, 27 … Pl. תְּמִימִין, תְּמִימֵי. Targ. Prov. XIII, 6. Ib. XXVIII, 10.”

doctrine.statement: What was brought to Yahweh’s altar had to be תָּמִים: “it shall be תָּמִים to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it”, for a blemished animal “will not be accepted for you” (Lev 22:20–21). So the Passover lamb (Exo 12:5), the red heifer (Num 19:2), and the lambs of the עֹמֶר and of the fiftieth day in Lev 23:12 and 18. Peter says believers were redeemed not with silver or gold but “with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish (ἀμώμου) and without spot” (1Pe 1:18–19); Hebrews, that Christ “through the eternal spirit offered himself without blemish to God” (Heb 9:14), one “tempted in all points like us, yet without sin” (Heb 4:15), who “did no sin” (1Pe 2:22); and Paul, that “Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us” (1Co 5:7). From the verses: the whole animal the law required showed what God would accept, a life with no sin in it, and only Christ’s was such; and those redeemed by it are to be presented “holy and without blemish” before him (Eph 5:27; Col 1:22).

Yahweh says to Abraham, “walk before me and be תָמִים” (Gen 17:1), and to Israel, “you shall be תָּמִים with Yahweh your God”, against seeking omens and the dead (Deu 18:9–14). Noah was “a righteous man, תָּמִים in his generations” (Gen 6:9), and Job “תָּם and upright” (Job 1:1), who held fast his תֻּמָּה when everything was taken from him (Job 2:3, 9). Neither was sinless: Noah lay drunk (Gen 9:21) and Job repented in dust and ashes (Job 42:6); David says “I was תָמִים with him, and kept myself from my iniquity” (Psa 18:24). With such a man Yahweh shows himself whole (Psa 18:26), and the psalmist asks to be kept from presumptuous sins, “then I shall be whole” (Psa 19:14). Jesus closes his command to love enemies and pray for persecutors, so as to be sons of the Father, with “you shall be perfect (τέλειοι), as your heavenly Father is perfect” (Mat 5:44–48), in the words the Septuagint uses for Deu 18:13; Luke’s account has “be merciful, as your Father is merciful” (Luk 6:36); and Paul asks the Philippians to be “children of God without blemish” in a crooked generation (Php 2:15). From the verses: to be תָּמִים is a heart undivided toward God, shown in keeping from sin and in dealing as he deals, not a claim to have no sin.

Moses calls Yahweh “the Rock, his work is תָּמִים, for all his ways are justice” (Deu 32:4); David, “as for God, his way is תָּמִים”, and he it is who “makes my way תָמִים” (Psa 18:31, 33); “the law of Yahweh is תְּמִימָה, restoring the soul” (Psa 19:8). James calls it “the perfect law of liberty” in which a man who looks and continues is blessed in his doing (Jas 1:25). From the verses: the wholeness asked of man is first God’s own, in his works, his way and his word, and it is he who makes a man’s way whole.

note: Drafted 2026-11-11 for Leviticus 23 (תָּמִים, Lev 23:12, 18; תְּמִימֹת, 23:15). The Thummim (Exo 28:30 etc.) is kept as a sense of תֹּם, since BDB’s key w.az.ab counts its tokens there and a key may name one word only; review whether it should be a word of its own. BDB key w.az.ab also counts qal infinitives of the verb (Lev 25:29; Num 14:33; 32:13; Deu 2:14; Jos 4:10; 5:6; 2Sa 15:24; 1Ki 6:22; 14:10; Jer 1:3; 36:23; 37:21), so its use count is high by about a dozen; w.az.ad (תָּם) likewise shares Gen 25:27, Pro 13:6 and Job 1:8; 8:20; 9:20, 22 with w.az.ab, and Exo 36:29 with w.ad.ac (תאם). w.aw.ak, a zero-token cross-reference, is left out. מְתֹם’s key counts Deu 2:34 and 3:6, which are מְתִם “men” (m.ea.aa), not this word. Left out: the name יוֹתָם (Jotham, “Yahweh is whole”), which belongs in names/; and the root תמה “be astonished”, which Wiktionary lists beside these but which is a separate root. Peshitta: SEDRA root 1976 ܬܡ, lexeme 3407 ܬܡܝܡܐ (Mat 10:16; Rom 16:19; Php 2:15), found via the BFBS word list; Payne Smith p. 614 (Dukhrana page image 0623, read) gives “innocent, perfect, harmless, guileless … Pael to make entire, to perfect … Ethpa. to become innocent”, but the Peshitta uses only the adjective in the New Testament, and renders Mat 5:48 τέλειοι by ܓܡܝܪܐ and 1Pe 1:19 and Heb 9:14 by another word, so those verses are not cited for the Syriac. No merged letters in the root. Krahmalkov pp. 492–493 read from the local PDF’s text layer only; page image unverified (no renderer available). Not entered: Egyptian tm “be complete” (TLA tla172000), which shares the meaning but is not Semitic and is not a loan in either direction; Sabaic ṯmm “there” (Biella p. 545, OCR only; a different root) and Sabaic tymm “in perpetuity” (Biella, OCR only, Biella herself unsure of the reading); Akkadian tamû “swear” (unrelated). Not consulted: DULAT and Ugaritic texts for a cognate (none in Segert’s glossary), Geʿez (Dillmann, Leslau). Open questions for review: (1) the gloss “whole” rather than the stock “perfect”; (2) the reading of Lam 3:22; (3) 1Sa 14:41 kept as a sense of תָּמִים with the Thummim as kin; (4) Exo 26:24 and 36:29 kept under תָּם though they may belong to תאם.
